items.title: Howard Alden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Kenny Davern I play a completely different way with when I play with him.

ctx.x: Well I was reading through the list of people you’ve played with and it’s pretty extensive. I would imagine you have to be versatile enough to figure out what this particular person is going to need from a guitar player.

That’s exactly right. Definitely. Being a guitar player and being in the rhythm section I get called to play with a lot of different people, more so than a horn player I think, because a horn player is either going to be a soloist, or part of a group sometimes, but usually either a major soloist or else play in a section in a big band. So I tend to get called to play in a lot of small groups with different people. Joe Bushkin again wanted one thing out of a guitar player, which was thrilling to play with him,…
Is it possible to be specific about that?

items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: In fact we’re going to do it tonight, the Breezin’ Along group. I’ll have fun with that. Because Howard Alden can read my mind

ctx.x: That’s something to sustain a band like that too without a bass player I think.

Oh we were brilliant. We really enjoyed. I made a conscious effort to play trios. So I did a trio with Art Hodes and Don DeMicheal, and then they died. And then it was Ralph Sutton and Gus Johnson and Gus Johnson died. Then I did one with Dick Wellstood and Bobby Rosengarden, and Dick died. And then, you know, but after a while, so like I switched to guitars. And they’re all alive. In fact we’re going to do it tonight, the Breezin’ Along group. I’ll have fun with that. Because Howard Alden can read my mind, Bucky…
